why: A capability frame is written in vendor marketing language; a solicitation is written by a contracting officer. Measured 2026-08-06: all eight of apexanalytix's approved core terms matched ZERO of 330,641 stored notices, while their federal equivalents matched hundreds. These groups let one approved term be MATCHED as the word a contracting officer actually writes, without editing the operator-owned frame.
law: Equivalence only, never association. 'supplier' and 'vendor' name the same thing in federal procurement text; 'payment' and 'invoice' do not. A group that merely relates two concepts widens the search into a different market and is the failure this file exists to avoid. Additions are cheap and reversible; a wrong group is a silent recall of the wrong records.

groups.note: used interchangeably in federal AP and procurement text
AP is the near-universal federal abbreviation
the Payment Integrity Information Act is the law ABOUT improper payments; a frame saying one must reach the other
riverbed class: the federal word is monitoring

REPLACES the onboarding/registration group, removed 2026-08-06. 'registration' alone matched SAM ENTITY REGISTRATION boilerplate in every Army construction notice, which poisoned term discovery's seed set. The file's own law is equivalence, never association: onboarding and registration are not the same act in federal text.

tiers.why: Adopted from the external Apex benchmark (2026-08-07). An EXACT phrase names the subject and may qualify a record on its own. An ADJACENT phrase is real domain language but too broad to qualify alone: it needs a second signal (NAICS boundary, a validated entity span, or an exact phrase) before a record is promoted. Collapsing the two is how a search becomes broad enough to be noisy and narrow enough to miss the market at the same time.
